stem:
Uday stirs a spoon of sugar into a glass of water. Soon no sugar grains can be seen, yet the water tastes sweet throughout the glass.

Which statement best explains this?

options.text: The sugar particles spread into the spaces between the water particles, so sugar is present throughout the water.
The sugar particles gather only at the top of the water, and only that top layer tastes sweet.
The sugar vanishes completely, and only a sweet taste remains with no sugar particles left.
Each water particle takes a sugar particle inside itself, which makes that water particle sweet.

teacher.key_rationale: Dissolved sugar particles occupy spaces among water particles and remain present, so the whole glass tastes sweet. A floating melt layer judges from a surface look. Saying sugar vanishes drops the particles-still-present condition. Swallowing sugar into water particles conflates dissolving with a different mechanism.
